title: What to Do When You Receive an FBR Penalty Notice
metaDescription: A calm, practical guide to handling an FBR penalty notice in Pakistan — how to verify it, respond within the window, fix the cause, and prevent the next one.
keywords: fbr penalty notice what to do
content:
Don't panic — work the steps

Receiving an FBR penalty notice is stressful, but it is a process you can work through calmly. Most notices trace back to a specific, fixable cause — often a silent POS submission failure the business never noticed — and a measured response usually leads to a far better outcome than either ignoring it or paying blindly. Here is how to handle one.

Step 1: Verify the notice

Read it closely and check what it is actually for. Compare its claim against your own records and the IRIS dashboard. Sometimes the issue is real; sometimes it is a discrepancy you can quickly explain or disprove with your data.

Step 2: Find the cause

If the notice points to unreported sales, look for the reason: an expired POS token, an offline queue that never synced, or a tax-mapping error. Identifying the root cause shapes both your response and your fix. The common FBR POS issues guide covers the usual suspects.

Step 3: Respond within the window

  1. Gather your records — POS data, invoices, filings for the period.
  2. File an appeal or response within the stated window, often around 30 days.
  3. Correct the underlying issue and document the fix.
  4. Pay or contest as advised, based on whether the penalty is justified.

Step 4: Prevent the next one

A penalty notice is a signal to tighten your routine. Fix the cause, then add a monthly reconciliation against the IRIS dashboard so the same silent gap cannot build up again. Most businesses that get one notice never get a second once they adopt the habit.

A real example

A retailer who received a notice for unreported sales traced it to an expired token, re-submitted the affected invoices, appealed within the window, and had the penalty reduced. The monthly check they added afterward has kept them clear since.

Stay clear going forward

faqs.question: What is the first thing to do with an FBR penalty notice?
faqs.answer: Read it carefully and verify the details against your own records and the IRIS dashboard. Confirm what it is actually for before responding — some notices stem from issues you can quickly disprove or fix.

faqs.question: How long do I have to respond?
faqs.answer: Notices usually specify a window, often around 30 days. Missing it removes your chance to contest or correct, so act promptly even if you intend to dispute.

faqs.question: Can I get a penalty reduced?
faqs.answer: Often, yes — by fixing the underlying cause, filing any appeal within the window, and showing corrected compliance. Acting quickly and in good faith works in your favour.

faqs.question: How do I avoid the next notice?
faqs.answer: Find and fix the root cause — frequently a silent POS submission failure — and add a monthly reconciliation so the same gap cannot recur unnoticed.
